category_title: Students with advanced decoding skills disengaged by traditional print media
student_description: Harry is a student whose advanced literacy skills are masked by his active resistance to traditional print media and conventional writing tasks, which he finds boring and refuses to do. He requires digital tools, multimedia activities, and personalized content creation to reveal his true abilities and engage deeply with literacy.

criteria.rationale: Harry perceives traditional print and paper-based writing as boring and will shut down, but he engages deeply when using digital apps or multimedia tools.
criteria.check: The tutor's immediate response must introduce a digital tool (e.g., an app, tablet) or a multimedia format (e.g., filming, voice recording) rather than insisting on traditional paper-and-pencil or standard print books.

criteria.rationale: Harry engages more creatively when he can personalize his learning through open content rather than completing rigid, conventional exercises.
criteria.check: The tutor must provide an opportunity for Harry to generate or select his own content (e.g., choosing photos, creating a story, acting out a scene) rather than answering pre-set questions.

criteria.rationale: Harry's success and high scores on digital platforms can be leveraged to build his confidence and willingness to engage with traditional print.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly use Harry's demonstrated success on a digital or alternative task as a bridge to encourage or reintroduce a traditional reading task.
